audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4..6].side read Yone on all three rows while win[4..6] read Anivia and the packet chart agrees with win[].
audit.why: The lane flips at Glacial Storm; phases[4].why already says 'Yone must respect every stun line now' while the side said Yone.
Yone's real spikes are the Mortal Steel two-stack dash from level 1, Spirit Cleave on a flat 14s, and Fate Sealed at 6 (120/100/80s). Anivia flips at 6 and again at Rod of Ages/Seraph's.
audit.corrected: Named the abilities behind each spike instead of describing them generically.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fabricated mechanics: Soul Unbound is repeatedly called an 'E-mark' used as a gap-closer ('E-Q dash combo lets him close the gap'), and the passive is described as 'crit resets every basic ability'. Neither exists.
audit.why: Riot text: Soul Unbound sends his spirit out with bonus move speed and then FORCES him back to his body, repeating a portion of the damage — it is a commitment that returns him to where he started, not a mark and not a gap-closer. Way of the Hunter is magic damage on every second attack plus increased crit chance, with no ability resets. The gap-closer is Mortal Steel at two Gathering Storm stacks.
audit.corrected: Gap-close is Mortal Steel's two-stack dash and knock-up; Soul Unbound is the punish window because his body is the target and he is dragged back to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the page never named a single Yone ability. Spirit Cleave's shield was also never mentioned.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave is a 14s shield that scales with champions hit — it eats the front of your burst, so it has to be baited before you spend Flash Frost.
audit.corrected: Mortal Steel, Spirit Cleave, Soul Unbound and Fate Sealed now all appear, with the shield stated in breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[0].

edits.before: Yone wins by landing Soul Unbound, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Yone wins by knocking you up with Mortal Steel, shielding through the answer with Spirit Cleave, then Fate Sealed.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Crystallize has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Soul Unbound: 22s at rank 1 — his spirit leaves the body behind, so the body is the target; stun it and he is dragged back into your storm. - Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s: bait it with Frostbite first. - Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the snap-back — Soul Unbound drags him to where he started, and a wall behind that spot ends him.

edits.before: Yone spends Soul Unbound early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Chilled targets take double Frostbite — storm first, and his shield covers half of it.

edits.before: That’s Yone’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Spirit Cleave comes back every 14s and shields more per champion it hits.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Two Mortal Steel hits arm the knock-up dash — deny him the second and he has no engage.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Yone walks straight at you.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in its line and drags them back — at max range that is always you.

edits.before: Yone's E-mark plus Q dash lets him punish your immobility for free early trades, so the early levels favor him.
edits.after: Mortal Steel's third cast dashes in with a knock-up, punishing your immobility for free trades early on.

edits.before: Passive crit resets and knockup follow-ups keep compounding his damage lead through level 3-5.
edits.after: Spirit Cleave shields him while every second attack adds magic damage, compounding his lead into 3-5.

edits.before: Same dash-punish pattern continues to define the lane as he keeps forcing all-ins on cooldown.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is down to 16s at rank 3, and every trade he opens still ends in the Q3 knock-up.

edits.before: Yone hits Q3 (knockup) plus E-mark combos and can dash through your Flash Frost to punish any Q you whiff, chunking you before you have Wall to peel.
edits.after: Yone hits the Q3 knock-up and Soul Unbound repeats his damage on the snap-back, chunking you for whiffing Flash Frost before Crystallize is up.

edits.before: Yone's E-Q dash combo lets him close the gap on your immobile kit almost instantly, and his passive crit steel resets every basic ability giving him repeatable burst you simply can't out-trade at levels 1-2. He punishes any Q Flash Frost whiff by dashing straight through it for free damage, and his knockup on Q3 sets up follow-up damage before you can react with Wall. Play passive, ward the river for his all-in timing, and just farm safely under tower rather than trying to contest CS.
edits.after: Mortal Steel's two-stack dash closes the gap on your immobile kit almost instantly, and Spirit Cleave shields him back up every 14 seconds, giving him repeatable trades you simply can't out-trade at levels 1-2. He punishes any Flash Frost whiff by walking through it for free damage, and the Q3 knock-up sets up follow-up damage before you can react with Wall. Play passive, ward the river for his all-in timing, and just farm safely under tower rather than trying to contest CS.

edits.before: Survive levels 1-5 without eating a full E-Q3 combo
edits.after: Survive levels 1-5 without eating a full Q3 knock-up

edits.before: Force short trades using E mark + Q dash to punish immobile poke
edits.after: Force short trades with Spirit Cleave shielding the poke he eats

notes: The page invented two Yone mechanics: an 'E-mark' gap-closer and passive crit resets on his basic abilities. Riot's text says Soul Unbound leaves his body behind and forces his spirit BACK to it — the opposite of a gap-closer, and the reason his body is the thing you stun. Way of the Hunter is magic damage every second attack plus crit chance, no resets. Fixed the packet defect that no Yone ability was ever named. Level chart squared to the packet on rows 5-7.
